title: Review of c06's pcell yield-selection finding: replicated on seed 7 (low-yield share 0.49 -> 0.19, neutral 0.49 -> 0.51), but mostly through particles per cell, not cell divisions
summary: Fresh seed 7 with c06's comp.py (nkinds=2, T=16000) and a labkit run of the y2=0.7 world. The low-yield (y=0.7) particle share in cells falls 0.49 -> 0.19 while the neutral arm drifts 0.49 -> 0.51, and pure low-yield cells stay small (median 97-104 particles against ~350 for pure high-yield cells), as the finding says. In this seed, though, the share shift is carried mostly by particles per cell (3.5x) and by mixed cells purifying, not by differential division: labkit records only 2 persistent splits (t~8600 and t~12700, max generation 1) after the share had already dropped to 0.18 by t=8000; at t=16000 there are 17 pure high-yield and 10 pure low-yield cells (neutral arm 10 and 12). Cell deaths are again essentially absent. The finding's own conclusion (colonization-phase, kinds assigned at seeding, not L7) stands.

observations.I: rerun/seed7/particles.png: ~26 walled cells persist t=1400-16000 (labkit: 26 components final, 26 persistent tracks), small cyan (kind-1, y=0.7) cells and large white (kind-0) cells; seed7_selection.png: kind-1 share 0.49 -> 0.19 vs neutral 0.51

verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed. On seed 7 the particle-share shift is mostly a cell-size effect (high-yield cells hold 3.5x more particles) plus purification of mixed cells; only 2 persistent cell splits occurred, both after t=8000, so 'selected by differential division' is not what drives this seed. Pure-cell counts 17:10 (y=0.7) vs 10:12 (neutral). I did not rerun the gate-off ablation or the genealogy tool.
